questions.question: Differentiate hypovitaminosis and avitaminosis.
questions.solution_html:
• Liberal valuation Definitions- (1.5 marks) each
  • Key Points: Hypovitaminosis is a partial deficiency or low level of a vitamin;
  • Avitaminosis is a severe or total lack of a specific vitamin leading to clinical disease (e.g.
  • Scurvy).
  • Explanatory summaries for any 6 questions ((5 marks) each).
  • • 23. Explain how poor nutrition during adolescence affects adult life.
  • Any 5 relevant points with explanation- (1 mark) each
  • o Adolescence is a critical growth phase. Poor nutrition can lead to stunted physical
  • growth, reduced bone density (increasing osteoporosis risk later), and a higher
  • predisposition to chronic diseases like obesity, diabetes, and heart disease in
  • adulthood.
  • • 24. Explain why older adults are more susceptible to nutritional problems.
  • Liberal valuation
  • Any 5 relevant points with explanation- (1 mark) each
  • o Susceptibility is due to physiological changes (reduced metabolism, impaired
  • digestion), sensory decline (loss of taste/smell), dental issues, and social factors like
  • isolation or limited mobility that affect food access.
  • • 25. Comment on the importance of nutrition during third trimester of pregnancy.
  • Importance of nutrition in pregnancy- (1 marks); Importance of third trimester- (1 mark);
  • Additional nutritional requirements during third trimester and its relevance- (3 marks)
  • o The third trimester involves rapid foetal brain development and weight gain.
  • Adequate intake of calcium (for bones), iron (for blood volume), and DHA (for
  • brain/eyes) is vital to prevent low birth weight and maternal depletion.
  • • 26. Explain the role of Vitamin D in the human body. Mention its sources and the effects of
  • deficiency and excess intake.
  • Sources- (1 mark); Importance- (2 marks); deficiency diseases- (1 mark); excess intake- 1
  • mark
  • o Role: Essential for calcium absorption and bone mineralization. Sources: Sunlight
  • fatty fish, egg yolks. Deficiency: Rickets (children), Osteomalacia (adults). Excess
  • Hypercalcemia (calcium buildup in blood/kidneys).
  • • 27. Comment on various antibodies in colostrum.
  • Liberal valuation
  • Any 5 relevant points related to colostrum and its importance- (1 mark) each
  • o Colostrum (the first breast milk) is rich in Secretory IgA, which provides passive
  • immunity by coating the infant's gut to prevent pathogens from entering. It also
  • contains IgG and IgM to support the developing immune system.
  • • 28. Define childhood and mention the age groups included under childhood nutrition.
  • Definition- (1 mark); mention each of 4 groups with brief explanation- (1 mark) each
  • o Childhood is the developmental period from infancy to the onset of puberty. Age
  • groups include Infancy (0-1 year), Toddlerhood (1-3 years), Preschool (3-5 years)
  • and School-age (6-12 years).
  • • 29. An elderly patient with severe vomiting is admitted to the hospital. Suggest an adequate
  • hydration strategy with reasons.
  • Liberal valuation- Give full marks if logical points related to elderly hydration is given
  • o Strategy: Immediate Intravenous (IV) fluids (like Normal Saline or Ringer's Lactate)
  • followed by gradual Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS). Reason: Severe vomiting causes
  • rapid electrolyte loss; elderly patients have lower total body water and are at high risk
  • for kidney failure if not rehydrated quickly.
  • • 30. Explain "Nutrition is a powerful tool for controlling diabetes mellitus."
  • Importance of nutrition in controlling Diabetes- (2 marks); various food examples
  • for diabetes patients- (2 marks); logical explanations- (1 mark).
  • o Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) focuses on controlling blood glucose levels
  • through low-glycemic index foods, high fiber, and portion control. Proper nutrition
  • reduces reliance on medication and prevents complications like neuropathy and
  • retinopathy.
